This diff adds `Bash(git merge *)` and `Bash(git merge-tree *)` to allowed-tools (line 7), and the body instructs building `git merge <theirs>` (line 38) directly from the `ours`/`theirs` branch-name args (the body's `git rev-parse <named-ref>` at line 51 is NOT allowlisted and would prompt; `git merge` alone carries the exploit). Git ref names may legally contain shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks) — only whitespace/control chars and `~^:?*[\` are rejected by `git check-ref-format`. Since the harness's Bash allowlist match is a literal-prefix/wildcard match over the whole command string (not an argv array), a branch named e.g. `pwn$(touch$IFS/tmp/pwned)` turns the model-issued command `git merge pwn$(touch$IFS/tmp/pwned)` into shell command substitution that executes BEFORE git even runs, executing arbitrary code with the session's privileges — regardless of whether the merge itself succeeds. Attack math: 1 attacker action (create/rename a git branch with a metacharacter payload, no push access to `ours` needed — only the ability to have that branch exist locally/on a shared remote as `theirs`), 1 `/merge-resolve` invocation naming it as `theirs` = full command execution, 0 retries required, cost = creating one git branch.

The gate's post-invocation check only verifies `.input.skill == $required` (skill NAME) from the transcript — it never checks `.input.args`. A lane/session under REQUIRE-SKILL can satisfy the gate by invoking `Skill(skill="<required>", args="<any other lane, or no args at all>")`, loading a different direction's (or the full, unnarrowed) context slice while every subsequent tool call is unconditionally allowed. This defeats the exact security promise the gate states in its own deny message ("your review context arrives via that invocation") and is untested by the bundled suite: cmd/tests/test_skill_invoke_gate.sh's skill_use() helper never sets `.input.args`, and its only negative case (test_wrong_skill_does_not_satisfy) checks a different skill NAME, not different args for the same skill.

Unlike merge-resolve's tightly scoped `Bash(git merge *)`, `git *` has no subcommand restriction, and several ordinary-looking git subcommands accept a `-c <key>=<value>` config override that runs an arbitrary shell command as a side effect of a routine operation. Reproduced: `git -c core.fsmonitor='sh -c "id > /tmp/pwned_marker"' status` executed the shell command and wrote `/tmp/pwned_marker` (verified: `cat /tmp/pwned_marker` printed the `id` output) via a completely ordinary `git status` call — no pager, no TTY, no special setup required (this is git's documented `core.fsmonitor` hook mechanism, not a bug in a specific git build). policyBase() never checks whether the merge-base it resolves equals HEAD. Setting acdsl/policy.json's base_ref to "HEAD" (or any ref currently pointing at HEAD) makes isBoundary compute true (branch name != "HEAD") so CheckPolicy proceeds into surfaceDelta/ruleDelta instead of short-circuiting — but since base==HEAD every diagnostic path is vacuously empty. findings.claim: classViolations exempts any rule declaration tagged lifetime="task" from every policy check in ANY mode (free/gated/strict) whenever AllowTaskContracts is true, with no file-path restriction; the shipped default acdsl/policy.json sets allow_task_contracts:true, so gated/strict targets inherit the exemption by default and a rule in a non-editable scope can be silently neutered by tagging its declaration lifetime="task".

sync_settings.sh unconditionally dot-sources install.env as shell before any validation — a second, independently-reachable execution sink for the same unescaped-install.env RCE payload already confirmed as GV5-235 (install.sh). Reached every unattended nightly orchestrate run (skills/smine/smine-orchestrate/SKILL.md step 3 invokes it directly), not merely as a subprocess of install.sh's own sourcing.

The C14 requirement (casual audience defaults auto-apply to 'decide' unless the operator overrides it) can never fire under the actual deployed routine, because the shipped plist sets SMINE_AUTO_APPLY to the literal non-empty string "never", so run.sh's -z sentinel for 'operator never touched this knob' is always false.

The new Stage-3 orchestrate gate trusts $exit_status as proof of no prior failure, but $exit_status never absorbs $consolidate_status, so a failed /smine-consolidate run silently lets the new merge-to-main gate proceed — contradicting this diff's own comment 'Any failure leaves the manual-merge world intact.'

The diff adds a mandatory Step-5 checkpoint requiring `git rev-parse <named-ref>` and bumps allowed-tools specifically so unattended --allowedTools runs can execute the merge, but the updated allowlist has no pattern matching git rev-parse, so the newly-mandatory step cannot run unattended.

effectiveAllowlist() falls back, whenever policy.VerifierAllowlist is empty, to treating every verifier name in the base ref's registry.json as sanctioned for rebinding by any editable-scope rule — indistinguishable between an absent verifier_allowlist key and an explicit empty array, inverting the expected deny-by-default meaning of an empty allowlist.

Shipped default editable_scopes=[GOLANG,PYTHON,SHELL,SQL,JSON] covers only 3 of the 5 scopes actually declared in smine's own acdsl/rules.acdsl, including JSON — the scope of ACDSL-JSON-003, the rule that schema-checks acdsl/policy.json itself — so an attacker branch can freely remove/modify ACDSL-JSON-003 under nominal 'gated' mode with zero diagnostics.

Client.SessionIndex duplicates the entire per-item Session construction already present in the unchanged Client.SessionsById — field-for-field identical composite literals apart from GitBranch and where Cwd is cleaned.
The isDeveloperAudience split of the repos table body duplicates the exact same label-fallback expression verbatim in both branches instead of computing the display label once.

TestRepoLabel only tests Label at 0 chars (roundtrip) and 81 chars (rejected); the boundary value of exactly labelMaxLength (80 chars) is never exercised, so a future off-by-one would silently start rejecting valid 80-char labels with no test catching it.
peekIdentity() has an untested exit path: a live listener returning HTTP 200 with a non-JSON body (json.Decode error) is never exercised by TestStartPeek.

The skill-overlay step does a raw cp of the operator's skill-overrides.json to settings.local.json instead of projecting only the documented skillOverrides key, so any other key ever present in that source file becomes live unreviewed config for the nightly acceptEdits session.

New skill-eval-fexplore table row uses short model aliases {fable-5, opus-4-8} while the One-off model bake-off section ~74 lines below uses full ids for the same models, both added in this diff — distinct from known GV3-010 (missing backing files, same line).

chooseFolderWindows builds the PowerShell -Command script using Go's %q verb, which produces Go-style backslash escaping that PowerShell double-quoted strings do not honor — a prompt containing a literal double quote could close the PowerShell string early. Latent only: both current call sites pass fixed, quote-free prompts.

CheckPolicy's gated/strict self-management gate diffs only the 4 policySurface paths and rule-declaration marker lines — never a registered verifier's own source content — so tampering a verifier's pass/fail logic in place under its unchanged name and rule id produces zero diagnostics in gated or strict mode, defeating the self-management guarantee.

The new acdsl-policy-guard.sh PreToolUse hook is wired only to matcher "Write|Edit|NotebookEdit"; no PreToolUse hook matcher covers Bash. permissions.allow still contains an unconditional "Bash(cp *)" plus git add/commit, so a Bash cp + git commit sequence overwrites acdsl/policy.json (or any acdsl-governed file) with zero hook interception, in any policy mode.

The casual-audience (non-dev) branch of the repos table renders the repo name as plain text with no anchor, contradicting the spec's explicit requirement (change-nondev-automation.md:239, "non-dev table: Name column (linked) only"); a casual-audience user has no way to click through to /repos/{name}. This whole if/else split, including the unlinked casual branch, is newly introduced by this diff.

The new bootstrap section on /welcome's setup tab (form, since/extra-prompt inputs, #bootstrap-result) is unasserted by any test; TestWelcomeRendersAllChecks hits the same response body but checks none of the new bootstrap strings, and TestWelcomeBootstrapConcurrent only covers the 409-conflict path — the success paths of POST /welcome/bootstrap and GET /welcome/bootstrap/status are untested.

The casual-audience branch of the h2 ternary renders the exact same text ({{t "Projects"}}) as the h1 ternary two lines up, so a casual-audience user sees the heading "Projects" immediately followed by a second heading also reading "Projects" — the developer branch differentiates them ("Repos" vs "repos") but the casual branch does not.

session-mine.js's args contract adds model?/effort? as a documented per-run agent-tier override, but the fronting skills/smine/smine/SKILL.md — the only documented invocation surface for /smine — never mentions model/effort anywhere: not in frontmatter, argument-hint, the Args section, or the Manual-run alternative's args object literal.

This new brief opens with an unparsed metadata line ("slug: applied-probe-safety") that no consumer strips — matrix.sh's brief_text="$(cat \"$brief\")" concatenates the whole file verbatim into the real fexplore session prompt, so the slug line ships as literal noise in front of the actual prompt.

writePolicy's schema-copy branch (policy.json present, policy.schema.json absent) is new in this diff and has zero test coverage — TestDistShipsPolicyModeRewritten always ships both files (real repo root) and TestWritePolicyNoSourceShipsNothing returns early before reaching the schema-stat line.

The new RUNNING badge (RUNNING) breaks the established two-class badge convention used everywhere else in the reviewed template set — every other badge pairs badge with a semantic modifier (badge-ok, badge-error, badge-dim).

The empty-state sentence is split across two separate {{t}} calls glued with a hardcoded space and "!", instead of the single-{{t}}-call-per-sentence pattern used everywhere else in this file — breaks word order for any language whose grammar doesn't match English's "happy <word>!" construction.

REPO_LOCAL_SETTINGS="$REPO_DIR/.claude/settings.local.json" is assigned identically in both the casual (line 277) and developer (line 293) branches of the new Skill-visibility block instead of once above the if/else — unnecessary duplication (ACTION-REVIEW-QUALITY-005).

LoadForSkill's flat-directory loop (236-246) and its new nested-run loop (248-263) duplicate the same body — filter by IsDir/pattern, call loadEvalDir, append to loadErrors, append to dirs — differing only in path/name construction.

sync_settings.sh:185-201 re-implements the exact hook-deployment loop that sync_hooks.sh:13-21 already owns, and install.sh invokes both back-to-back — hooks get copied twice per install and the two copies have already drifted (sync_settings.sh added a diff-skip; sync_hooks.sh alone has interactive-prune).

The ~25-30 line git-fixture-building 'shared content block' sequence is duplicated verbatim 4+ times across cmd/tests/test_remove_agent_worktrees.sh and cmd/tests/test_print_agent_worktrees_status.sh (including a third repeat within the latter alone), with no shared helper.
The new archived-folders table uses the shared checklist-table class but ships with no <thead>, unlike every other in-scope checklist-table use in this same commit.
The new DRIFT_SCHEMA uses snake_case property names, breaking the camelCase convention every untouched sibling schema (MINE_SCHEMA, DIM_SCHEMA, TRIM_SCHEMA) in this exact file uses.

handleTogglePermission never rejects a negative {index} path value — only `err != nil` and an upper bound (`index >= len(*source)`) are checked, so `entry := (*source)[index]` panics on a negative index, unlike hooks.go's sibling handlers which guard `err != nil || index < 0`.

The pre-invocation exemption `[ "$tool" = "Skill" ] && exit 0` allows the in-flight tool call through whenever it is ANY Skill invocation, with zero comparison to $required or tool_input.skill — a session under REQUIRE-SKILL whose first call is `Skill(skill="<some-other-skill>")` is silently allowed instead of denied, contradicting the hook's own stated contract. (Cited at line 45 by the lane; verified at the actual line 51 — a citation nit, not a substance error.)

`dev_mode="${SMINE_DEV_MODE:-}"` followed by `[[ -n "$dev_mode" ]] && PROMPT+=" --dev"` treats any non-empty value — including the string "0" — as true, so SMINE_DEV_MODE=0 (meant to disable dev mode) still threads --dev into the prompt. Duplicated identically in cmd/bootstrap/run.sh.

taskState/Start/Stop/RunNow build PowerShell -Command strings via fmt.Sprintf, embedding routine.Label (taken verbatim from the on-disk plist filename with zero character-set validation at Scan()/load() time) into a single-quoted PowerShell literal with no escaping. A plist filename containing a single quote and PowerShell metacharacters breaks out of the -TaskName argument and executes arbitrary PowerShell in the smine server's process/user context.

handleProfileStyleSave writes unvalidated, unauthenticated user-supplied content verbatim to ~/.claude/context/global/style-profile.md, which cmd/hooks/global-context.sh cats raw (no escaping, no trust marker) into the context of every future Claude Code session on the machine, including autonomous routines running in acceptEdits with real repo write/exec access — one unauthenticated POST stages a persistent prompt-injection payload.

smine-style rewrites the machine-global, every-session-injected style-profile.md wholesale from an LLM's distillation of up to 30 full session transcripts, with only a single prose 'Hard invariant' bullet — no mechanical scan — guarding against a pasted secret/credential/PII being echoed into that file, unlike every sibling proposal-writing skill in this diff which runs a deterministic validation pass before finishing.

The new isDeveloperAudience gate on a finding snippet's <summary> (developer sees Kind/Lang/Source, casual audience sees a generic 'technical detail' string) has no render test for the casual-audience branch anywhere in internal/server/*_test.go — only the developer-audience rendering is asserted.

reloadSessions (called from every session-page handler) silently degrades to stale state on Store.Reload() failure per its own doc comment, and that failure branch has zero test coverage anywhere in the suite.

TestSessionsById's meta-less case never asserts the resulting Session.Cwd, hiding that SessionsById unconditionally does filepath.Clean(item.Meta.Cwd) even when empty (Clean("")=="."), diverging untested from SessionIndex's explicit empty-Cwd guard.

mapInterval/mapIntervals/mapIntervalArray (new in this diff) each have an error branch with zero test coverage: mapInterval's uint64 type-assertion failure, mapIntervals' default type-mismatch case, mapIntervalArray's non-dict-item failure.

The empty-scope hint's gate changed from `{{if .Scope.MdReports}}` to `{{if and .Scope.MdReports isDeveloperAudience}}`, but no test renders this branch for a casual-audience profile with .Scope.MdReports > 0 to confirm the developer-only hint is actually suppressed for casual users.
The detail-mode squash_in comma-join over multiple candidate branches is completely unexercised — every existing squash fixture uses only a single candidate ('main').
TestDetectContextCoverage never exercises DetectContextCoverage's first read error branch (unreadable sourceIndexPath) — only the target-index-unreadable branch is covered.
